newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Simsen plans acquisitions, rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Simsen plans acquisitions, rights issue.

text.p: Simsen Metals (Holdings) Ltd said it would launch a HK$453.6 million rights issue to finance the HK$400 million acquisition of a Hong Kong property and the HK$120 million purchase of a metal and futures broking business.
The nonferrous metals trader said on Monday it had agreed to buy an option for HK$20 million to buy property holding company New Wise Enterprise Ltd.
New Wise owns the basement, shops one and two on the ground floor and the whole of the first, second and third floors of Cameron Commercial Centre on Hennessy Road in the Wan Chai district.
Simsen agreed to buy the holding company for HK$380 million and would arrange bank financing for HK$280 million and use the proceeds of the rights issue for the remaining HK$120 million.
Simsen said it had also agreed to buy Mankeen Management Ltd, a metal and futures broking and margin financing firm, for HK$120 million.

Mankeen holds properties in Hong Kong, a Securities and Futures Commission commodities trading licence, one share in the Hong Kong Futures Exchange and membership on the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society.
Simsen said it had also bought an option for US$300,000 to buy three percent of the issued share capital of Smelter Co, a firm in the process of incorporation in Oman, the Middle East.
Smelter is to develop and operate a complex consisting of an aluminium smelter, a power plant and a water desalination plant. Its proposed total share capital is intended to be US$600 million.
Simsen said the company was expected to be listed on the Muscat Securities Market on or before January 31, 1998.

Simsen said it proposed to raise HK$453.6 million before expenses through a rights issue of 504 million new shares in the proportion of two rights shares for every one existing share at an issue price of HK$0.90 per rights share.
Simsen said the acquisition of Mankeen Management and a stake in Smelter Co would expand its future earnings base and strengthen its asset base.
"The property is intended to house the group's headquarters and certain of its broking operations," it said in a statement.
"After completion of the proposed acquisitions, the group will be able to carry on the core business in the People's Republic of China and to expand into the Middle East."
Simsen Metals shares began trading on Monday for the first time since being suspended on April 18.
The shares were up HK$0.15 at HK$1.20 in early trade.
